name: Spatial Orientation
definition: The ability to know your location in relation to the environment or to know where other objects are in relation to you.

benchmarks_mapped.name: Habitat Challenge PointNav (Realistic PointNav, 2020/2021 setting: no GPS+Compass, noisy RGB-D and actuation)

benchmark.name: Habitat Challenge 2020 PointNav
benchmark.model_or_system: DAN / SLAM-net with D* planning (Karkus et al.)
benchmark.metric: SPL (success weighted by path length), percentage points (0-100)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult navigating an unfamiliar indoor building from an egocentric view. They are given the goal as coordinates relative to where they started, with noisy movement and no GPS or compass.

benchmark.name: Habitat Challenge 2021 PointNav
benchmark.model_or_system: VO for Realistic PointGoal (Partsey et al.; learned policy + visual odometry)
benchmark.metric: SPL (Success weighted by Path Length), 0-1 scale reported x100
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population: people who navigate unfamiliar indoor buildings to a target described by relative coordinates, using only first-person vision and self-motion cues (dead reckoning), with no map or compass.

benchmark.name: Habitat Challenge PointNav (Realistic PointNav, 2020/2021 setting: no GPS+Compass, noisy RGB-D and actuation)
benchmark.model_or_system: VO for Realistic PointGoal (Partsey et al., 'Is Mapping Necessary for Realistic PointGoal Navigation?', CVPR 2022)
benchmark.metric: SPL (Success weighted by Path Length), percentage (x10^2)
benchmark.human_reference: General working adults with normal vision doing egocentric navigation in unfamiliar indoor spaces. Examples: delivery, facilities, security or field staff finding a location from a relative displacement ('go ~8 m ahead and ~3 m left of where you started') without a map, GPS or markers.

benchmark.name: SQA3D
benchmark.metric: EM@1 exact-match accuracy (%) on SQA3D test
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. The published baseline comes from amateur, non-expert participants answering situated spatial questions in 3D scenes.

benchmark.name: VSI-Bench
benchmark.metric: average accuracy across the 8 VSI-Bench tasks (%; multiple-choice accuracy plus mean relative accuracy for numeric tasks)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. Egocentric spatial orientation in everyday indoor scenes is a general ability, not a specialist skill.

benchmark.name: VSI-Bench
benchmark.model_or_system: SpaceMind (dual encoder: VGGT spatial encoder + InternViT, fine-tuned)
benchmark.metric: VSI-Bench overall average score (%): mean of 8 subtasks; multiple-choice tasks scored by accuracy, numeric tasks by mean relative accuracy
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. Spatial orientation in everyday indoor environments is a general human capability, not a specialist skill.

benchmark.name: VSI-Bench
benchmark.metric: VSI-Bench overall average (%): macro-average of multiple-choice accuracy and mean relative accuracy on numerical tasks, across 8 tasks
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday spatial orientation: navigating indoor spaces and judging where objects are relative to oneself. No specialist training is assumed.
